summary: User seeks guidance on running cleanup logic (defers) when FailWorkflow panic policy is triggered by non-deterministic errors in long-running workflows.
userImpact: Users running long-running agent workflows with FailWorkflow policy cannot properly clean up resources when non-deterministic errors occur, causing incomplete cleanup and workflows to appear running when they've actually failed.
rootCause: When non-determinism is detected, the workflow cannot restore its state or generate new commands, so the workflow code may not even execute to the point where defers are called.
proposedFix: Use child workflows with a parent workflow that runs compensation logic for cleanup operations.
workaround: Restructure workflows as child workflows with parent compensation logic handling cleanup and notifications.
keyQuote: If you want to run some logic after a workflow fails the best way currently is to run your workflow as a child workflow and have the parent run any compensation.
